title: Scheduled runs become governed, tool-using Do runs with a stored approval contract, non-delegable tools, result delivery and origin attribution
summary: Replace the single no-tool 1,024-token call in ExecuteScheduledStep with a normal budgeted Do run started by the Temporal supervision, seeded with context. At schedule creation the owner signs a consent card whose approved capabilities are stored with an expiry; at run time an effect proceeds only if covered and delegable, otherwise the run drafts and notifies off-surface (without an Allow button for high-risk tools). Deliver results ('See results'), and tag runs with origin.
whyItMatters: Scheduled agents are near-universal (10 of 12) and the Agents pages promise them, but each Verevon step is a stateless completion. The owner ruling of 2026-09-28 (draft-only) is compatible with this design: the stored contract can start as read plus draft-only and widen later by explicit decision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (cron jobs as full agent runs with skills, context chaining, multi-platform delivery and an at-most-once ledger) ; Claude (scheduled tasks store approvedPermissions with expiry, a non-delegable tool set, and notifications that drop the Allow action for high-risk tools) with Hermes (headless modes deny by default with a narrowed toolset and auto-pause on injection hits)
others: Manus (schedule model with expiry and run target)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-04-05: 10 of 12 sources (table-stakes); origin and status attribution 4 of 12 | R-t3-11-04: unattended policy 4 of 12 (common); off-surface approvals 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Schedule{rrule|cron, tz, prompt, model, skills, autonomy_cap, run_target new_thread|same_thread, expiry}. Each schedule stores approvedPermissions [{tool, rule, expiresAt}] captured at creation;

reference.corrections: (1) Claude's stored shape is approvedPermissions[{toolName, ruleContent?, approvedAt}], not {tool, rule, expiresAt}: expiry is computed at check time from an admin-managed lifetime (mcpScheduledTaskApprovalLifetimeDays). (4) Prevalence 10/12 is broadly right but counts the same vendor twice (manus + web-manus, claude + web-claudeai). DeepSeek's feature is follow-up reminders that are off by default in Desktop, and Antigravity's Windows schedules run only while the app or daemon is alive. Origin attribution '4 of 12' also double-counts Manus.

title: Real Agents and Automations hubs: versioned agent definitions, named agents, automations with run now and pause, and a working Fleet console
summary: Introduce a versioned agent definition (name, instructions, tool allowlist bound to capability ids, model policy, autonomy cap, knowledge scope, schedules, owner and Space scope) in the capability registry and use it three ways: selectable roles for subagents, a builder with sandbox preview, and persistent named agents with their own thread and memory. Turn the agent pages from design previews into hubs over owner-plane resources, add an Automations hub over /api/v1/cron with Active/Paused/Completed and Run now/Pause/Edit, and fix the Fleet console, which calls a route that does not exist.
whyItMatters: The audit is about the chat and agent pages, and the agent pages are largely blueprints: preset agents have empty action sets, the workflow builder and chatbot studio are previews, and the fleet console has no backend route. Perplexity and Manus show hubs; Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT Workspace Agents show definitions and builders.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity web (hubs for tasks, connectors, automations with Active/Paused/Completed and Run now/Pause/Edit/Pin/Delete, skills, memory) plus Manus (Agents tab, Automations panel) ; Manus (named persistent agents with their own email, phone, computer and skills) for identity; Cursor (agent definition files with tools, model and permission mode) for roles; ChatGPT Workspace Agents (versioned spec, preview, deployment with activity log) for the builder
others: Cursor (team-published named agents pinned to member sidebars)
Perplexity (Computer from forwarded email, Slack-bound projects)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-12-04: 3 of 12 sources (differentiator). | R-t3-04-06: persistent named agents 5 of 12 (common); custom roles 2 of 12; builder and deployment 2 of 12; non-app entry points 4 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Each hub is a list over an owner-plane resource with a state filter and row actions bound to typed APIs. Agent{id, owner, persona, instructions, memory scope, skills, channels[], autonomy_cap, version}.

Phase 2: agent definition record and builder, with action sets populated from the typed action registry (F-t3-025). Phase 3: persistent named agents with scoped memory (F-t3-060).

Agent definitions already exist in the Application Plane Convex agents table (name, systemPrompt, model, tools, knowledgeBindings, embed) plus Space bindings with in-room create, bind, pause and revoke, but they are unversioned with string tool names, and subagent.task has no role parameter (agent.rs:4278).

Fleets are a Quarry/Control concept (quarry_fleets); no producer exists in Model Plane or the gateway, so a Fleet console needs a Quarry-audience BFF proxy and Quarry org scoping. Phase 2 should extend the Convex agents definition and Space binding (version history, tool allowlist as capability ids, autonomy cap) and have Model Plane consume the resolved definition at invoke time, as inject_mentioned_space_agent_persona already does for personas. Consolidate the two existing schedule UIs into the hub rather than adding a third.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Phase 1 alone (hub over existing PATCH/list, Fleet proxy or removal) is M; adding run-now plus run history is M more; versioned definitions, builder and persistent agents are the XL part.
verevon.verdictReason: Preview-only pages and the broken Fleet route are confirmed, but the item ignores the existing Convex agent definitions and Space agent flow, misplaces the definition store in capability-core, and understates the backend work behind Run now.

title: User and org memory controls: on, pause, reset and org policy
summary: Add a user memory state (on, paused, off) and a Reset all memory action, plus an org policy that can disable memory and the learning review, enforced in session-core at every place memory is written or read: the Dreaming loop, prefetch, save_memory, recall_memory and the skill review. Add an immediate in-chat 'remember this' path in Ask mode that confirms the save, refused under ZDR.
whyItMatters: Users and enterprise admins expect to be able to stop the assistant learning about them, and a product that learns by default needs this before it can be sold to Norwegian and EU buyers. It is table-stakes (9 of 12 sources) and today half built: you can view, correct and delete entries but not switch learning off or wipe it in one action. Raised to priority from the comparator's recommended because of the governance inconsistency described below.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude keeps topic-based entries saved during chat, each visible and editable, with 'remember' and 'forget' in chat, separate pause (keep rows, stop using and generating) and reset (erase) actions, an org opt-in on Team plans and a transcript indicator when memory is read or written. Perplexity lets the org owner switch derived features on or off for all members. Implementation shape: per-account flags generate and reference give on, paused and off; paused keeps rows but skips prefetch and extraction.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No user-level memory on, pause or off switch, no Reset all, no org-level memory policy found (bounded grep of Control Plane for memory_enabled, memoryPolicy, allow_memory found only the user-core settings above), and injection and extraction are unconditional server-side. Control Plane already models a memoryEnabled flag that defaults to false, yet nothing enforces it and the Model Plane learns regardless, so the stored setting and actual behaviour disagree. Ask-mode chat has recall_memory only; save_memory is Do-only.

approachOriginal: Use Control Plane as the single source of truth: reuse user-core AISettings (memoryEnabled, personalizationEnabled) and add an org policy {memory_allowed, member_default}. Deliver the decision to the Model Plane signed with the session or run decision (no cross-plane DB access), and enforce it in session-core in the Dreaming loop, memory_prefetch.rs, save_memory and recall_memory, and in the capability-core skill review (R-t3-08-03). States: on, paused (rows kept, prefetch and extraction skipped), off. Add a ResetMemory RPC that reuses memory_erasure.rs for both tiers. Frontend: toggles and Reset in MemorySection, an admin control in org settings, and a visible indicator on the turn when memory is read or saved (the memory_recall event already exists). Add a gateway write route for an immediate Ask-turn 'remember this' that returns a confirmation chip. Decide and document the default (the user-core default is off; the current Model Plane behaviour is on) and migrate existing users deliberately.
dependencies: Control Plane user settings and org policy
planeOwner: Model Plane (enforcement); Control Plane (settings and org policy); Frontend Plane (controls)
risks: A paused state must also stop the background extractor and the skill review, or memories and skills appear while paused. Changing the default affects existing users. ZDR orgs should be treated as memory-off for writes.

verevon.exactGap: Users can list, correct and delete memories (memory.rs:50-54; MemorySection.tsx:69; memory-client.ts:69-101) but there is no on/paused/off state, no Reset all and no org memory policy: user_memory_controls holds only extract_after and forgotten ids (0039_memory_user_control.sql:3-8), Dreaming is configured by env only (dreaming.rs:146-150), and the chat recall gate checks only conversation_only, web-only scope and trivial prompts (sse.rs:1655). Control Plane user-core already stores memoryEnabled (default false) and personalizationEnabled in AISettings (handlers.go:1405-1421) but nothing else in apps reads them, so the stored default (off) contradicts actual behaviour (learning on); Ask turns can recall but not save (inline_tool_allowed refuses save_memory, tool_loop.rs:639), and only per-turn exclusions exist (ZDR turns neither read nor write, zdr_features.rs:166; conversation_only skips extraction, dreaming.rs:223).
reuse: session-core user_memory_controls (add a state column) as the enforcement copy, instead of a new table
memory_erasure::erase_semantic_copies and the gdpr bulk erase (memory_erasure.rs:112; gdpr.rs:444) for Reset across both tiers
BFF stamping precedent apply_org_zdr_posture (shared.rs:95-117): a server-set field stripped from client bodies, for request-time recall and save gates
org_quota-style service-principal pull from org-core for org policy and for the Dreaming worker, which has no request context
user-core AISettings (memoryEnabled, personalizationEnabled) as the user preference store, once the default conflict is resolved
Existing per-turn gates to extend: conversation_only in sse.rs:1655 and dreaming.rs:223, memory_tool_preflight (runtime_loop/mod.rs:2125)
verevon.constraints: Memory data and learning are Model Plane (session-core) but user preference and org policy belong to Control Plane (CLAUDE.md:23), with no cross-plane DB reads: request-time paths can take a BFF-stamped server-set field, while the Dreaming worker and the skill/learning review run without a request and need a service-principal pull or a pushed projection. Pause must also gate the background extractor and the learning/skill review (session-core learning_events.rs and capability-core learning/reviewer.go exist per grep and were not re-read), otherwise memories or skills appear while paused. ZDR must propagate: ZDR turns already skip memory (zdr_features.rs:166), and ZDR orgs should be treated as memory-off for writes. Changing the default from today learning-on to the stored off value affects every existing user and needs a deliberate migration.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item's "signed with the session or run decision" is heavier than the codebase needs: use the BFF-stamp pattern for chat turns and a service-principal pull (org_quota.rs pattern) for Dreaming and learning review, or make session-core user_memory_controls the single enforcement copy written through a gateway route when the user toggles, keeping user-core AISettings.memoryEnabled as a mirror or retiring it so there are not two switches. Settle the memoryEnabled=false versus learning-on default before shipping. Keep the Ask-mode "remember this" path as a separate optional step.
verevon.effortNote: M for a user-level on/paused/off switch plus Reset (session-core state column, Dreaming and recall gates, gateway route, MemorySection controls). Org policy, learning-review gating and the Ask-mode remember path make the full item L.
verevon.verdictReason: Gap is accurate and verified (no switch, no reset, no org policy, stored flag unread), so the recommendation stands; the approach should reuse the BFF-stamp and org_quota pull patterns, and effort is larger than M once org policy and learning review are included.

title: Transcript performance: benchmark first, then block-level streaming render, a virtualised timeline and paged transcript reads

title: Prompt-cache discipline: measured hit rate, stable/context/volatile prompt tiers with an append-only tail, lineage-scoped cache keys and compaction transactions
summary: Turn on and measure what is built: enable the OpenAI stable-prefix order in staging, record cache read/write tokens and a cache-miss reason per route, then define a prompt-tier contract in mp-contracts for both loops (org and Space blocks in the shared prefix, per-user memory and volatile injections such as time, recall, skills and approved plan in an append-only tail), lineage-scoped cache keys, todo recitation in the tail, and compaction as a bracketed transaction with a visible marker.

title: Org and role model entitlements: Control Plane decides, Model Plane enforces at admission
summary: Give the refused allowed_models policy field a real owner: a Control Plane entitlement policy (org, role, group, plan) with allow/deny model lists, maximum effort, admin default model/effort per surface, and an explain endpoint for one member's effective access. Model Plane receives the resolved entitlement in the auth context, filters ListModels, and refuses disallowed models at admission with a typed reason, never silently substituting.
whyItMatters: Enterprise buyers expect to restrict expensive or non-EU models per role. The code itself flags this hole: the gateway refuses the allowlist by name because no service owns it, so operators currently cannot restrict models at all.

others: claude (152, per-role effort caps, most permissive role wins)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Admins set starting model, reasoning level and speed separately per surface; new models are off by default for enterprise; roles are additive (union of allows) and the most permissive effort cap wins; a Model Test tool shows a member's effective access. [DOC for ChatGPT, SRC for Claude desktop and Codex]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:148-160 (verified: allowed_models is the only policy field with no owner and is refused by name)
verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No per-org or per-role model allowlist, no role-level effort cap, no admin default per surface, no effective-access explainer. The privacy-tier floor in admission already fails closed but is not an entitlement system.

approachOriginal: Control Plane: policy schema {subject, allow_models[], deny_models[], max_effort, default_model, default_effort} with resolution (union of role allows, intersect with plan, most permissive effort cap) and an explain API. Model Plane: extend mp-authctx claims to carry the resolved entitlement; inference-core filters ListModels and enforces in admission next to the privacy-tier floor. Frontend Plane: admin page beside the router-policy page (apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs). The entitlement can only narrow access; it must never widen an owner-plane ACL or a Space's rights.
planeOwner: Control Plane (policy) with Model Plane (enforcement) and Frontend Plane (admin UI)
risks: Resolution order must be documented and tested; entitlement must not widen Space or owner-plane ACLs; stale cached entitlements could allow a revoked model.

verevon.exactGap: No per-org, per-role or per-plan model allowlist exists: OrgPolicy.allowed_models has no owning service and SetPolicy refuses it by name (grpc.rs:148-160; gateway.proto:1343-1357), the only live allowlist is the deployment-wide ALLOWED_MODELS env var applied in normalize.rs:360-384, and list_models ignores the caller claims (http_routes.rs:7603-7606; inference-core grpc.rs:394-424). There is also no effort cap, admin default per surface or effective-access explainer, and the Convex org settings mirror fields allowedModels and defaultModel are never read for Model Plane admission (convex schema.ts:19-23).

The org_quotas pull pattern: model-gateway org_quota::fetch_org_limits against org-core with a service principal (org_quota.rs:1-24, sse.rs:1154-1155, grpc.rs:2173-2215)

normalize.rs allowlist check as the single admission choke point (normalize.rs:360-384) and list_models, which already receives Claims (http_routes.rs:7603-7606)
Router-policy admin page and gateway proxy (router_policy.rs) as the UI neighbour
verevon.constraints: CLAUDE.md:23 assigns entitlements and quotas to Control Plane, so policy storage, resolution and the explain API belong in org-core (Go) with Model Plane only reading and enforcing; there is no cross-plane DB access, so enforcement needs a service-principal pull (org_quota.rs pattern) or a signed claim. Fail closed: the existing org_quota fetch deliberately fails OPEN on an org-core outage (sse.rs:1154), which is wrong for a deny list, so use last-known-good with a short TTL or refuse. An entitlement may only narrow access and must not widen a Space or owner-plane ACL. The router-policy admin gate is the SPA RequireWorkspaceAdmin plus a forwarded x-user-role header (router_policy.rs:9-10), which is not sufficient authority for an entitlement writer, so the write must be role-checked in org-core. ZDR: an allowlist must not silently remove every ZDR-attested model for a ZDR org, so admission should refuse with a typed reason rather than substitute a model.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Extend org-core (org_entitlements/org_quotas pattern) rather than a new Control schema, and say so. Enforce in model-gateway, which already owns the env allowlist in normalize.rs and receives Claims in list_models; inference-core ListModels takes only modality and provider and has no org input, so it is not the filter point (its chain selection may take the allowlist as defense in depth next to the privacy-tier floor). Deliver by short-TTL service-principal pull for lists (claims would bloat and go stale; the ZDR claim needs a 60 second TTL cap for exactly that reason) or add a compact policy version claim. Roles are not in mp-authctx Claims (claims.rs:10-38), so org-core must resolve role to allowlist before Model Plane sees it.
verevon.effortNote: M for an org-level allow/deny list with default model and ListModels filter using the org_quota pull pattern; role/group/plan resolution, effort cap and the explain endpoint make the full item L.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and unbuilt, so the item stands, but its placement is partly off (inference-core filter) and it omits the existing org-core entitlement and org_quota pull infrastructure that should be reused.
